answer: The farm's purse empties long before its list of names does. The manifest lists a name once it holds Chartered coppersmith registry entry, and an entry smiths keep after hammer inspections is the entry the clerk looks for. Each attempt carries a waiting period of 10 days that no payment can shorten, and the charge lands before any reward is even counted. Copying a name buys nothing here — each copy must pay the same toll again. Every basalt is counted once. The bridge is checked, not assumed. The clerk notes wharf.
